## 2. Consolidate culture records and reconcile AST results

The source contains repeated culture details across organism and antibiotic
rows. Create one record per culture, retain the original organism labels,
and reconcile each organism-antibiotic endpoint before applying organism
mappings or resistance classifications.

### 2.1 Create one record per culture

A culture is identified by its source release, patient, encounter, and order.
For each culture, retain an order-level field only when its source values
agree. If a field contains different values, including a mixture of a value
and missing data, set that field to missing and flag the culture for review.
The flag identifies a conflict; it does not automatically exclude the culture.

```{r consolidate-cultures}

culture_id = c(
  "source_version",
  "patient_key",
  "encounter_key",
  "culture_order_key"
)

organism_id = c(culture_id, "organism")

cultures =
  armd_staged %>%
  group_by(across(all_of(culture_id))) %>%
  summarise(
    source_row_count = n(),
    has_order_level_conflict = n_distinct(
      culture_time_shifted,
      ordering_mode,
      culture_description,
      was_positive
    ) > 1,
    across(
      c(
        culture_time_shifted,
        ordering_mode,
        culture_description,
        was_positive
      ),
      ~ if (n_distinct(.x) == 1) first(.x) else .x[NA_integer_]
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    cohort_id = case_when(
      culture_description == "BLOOD" ~ "blood",
      culture_description == "URINE" ~ "urine",
      culture_description == "RESPIRATORY" ~ "respiratory",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  )
```

`across()` applies the same consistency check to each of the four culture
fields. In the conflicting case, `.x[NA_integer_]` returns a missing value
with the field's original type, preserving date-time, character, and integer
types. `n_distinct()` includes missing values in its count by default.

### 2.2 Retain the original organism observations

Create one record per culture and original organism label, then attach the
consolidated culture details. These represent source organism observations;
ARMD does not supply verified biological isolate identifiers. The explicit
join keys prevent unrelated columns from affecting the match.

```{r create-culture-organisms}
culture_organisms =
  armd_staged %>%
  filter(!is.na(organism)) %>%
  select(all_of(organism_id)) %>%
  distinct() %>%
  inner_join(
    cultures,
    by = culture_id,
    na_matches = "never",
    relationship = "many-to-one"
  )
```

`na_matches = "never"` prevents missing identifiers from matching one another,
consistent with the existing SQL joins. `relationship = "many-to-one"`
requires each organism observation to match at most one culture record.

### 2.3 Reconcile repeated AST results

Group antibiotic records within each culture and original organism label.
Repeated identical results resolve to one result. Different results, including
a valid result combined with a missing value, remain conflicts. An endpoint
containing only missing values retains a missing status.

| Source values within an endpoint | Status | Retained result |
|---|---|---|
| Susceptible, Susceptible | resolved | Susceptible |
| Susceptible, Resistant | conflict | Missing |
| Susceptible, missing | conflict | Missing |
| Missing, missing | missing | Missing |

Rows without an antibiotic name do not define an AST endpoint. They remain
represented in the culture and organism data frames above.

```{r reconcile-source-ast}
ast_endpoints =
  armd_staged %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(organism),
    !is.na(antibiotic)
  ) %>%
  group_by(across(all_of(c(organism_id, "antibiotic")))) %>%
  summarise(
    source_result_rows = n(),
    missing_result_rows = sum(is.na(susceptibility)),
    result_state_count = n_distinct(susceptibility),
    candidate_result = first(susceptibility),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    resolution_status = case_when(
      result_state_count > 1 ~ "conflict",
      is.na(candidate_result) ~ "missing",
      TRUE ~ "resolved"
    ),
    susceptibility = if_else(
      resolution_status == "resolved",
      candidate_result,
      NA_character_
    ),
    repeated_result_rows = source_result_rows - result_state_count
  ) %>%
  select(-candidate_result) %>%
  semi_join(
    culture_organisms,
    by = organism_id,
    na_matches = "never"
  )
```

The candidate result is retained only when all source values agree, so the
resolved output is independent of source row order. The `semi_join()` keeps
endpoints linked to an existing organism observation without adding columns
or multiplying rows.

### 2.4 Inspect culture and AST summaries

Check how many cultures have conflicting fields, whether encounter identifiers
are missing, and how many AST endpoints are resolved, missing, or conflicting.
The source row total in `culture_check` should match the imported 2,241,050
rows. Culture counts are expected to be smaller because each source culture
may have many organism and antibiotic rows.

```{r check-culture-and-ast-results}
culture_check =
  cultures %>%
  summarise(
    culture_count = n(),
    source_rows_accounted_for = sum(source_row_count),
    cultures_with_conflicting_fields = sum(has_order_level_conflict),
    missing_encounter_keys = sum(is.na(encounter_key)),
    missing_culture_times = sum(is.na(culture_time_shifted))
  )

ast_check =
  ast_endpoints %>%
  count(resolution_status, name = "endpoint_count")

print(culture_check, width = Inf)
print(ast_check)

culture_organisms %>%
  count(cohort_id, name = "culture_organism_count", sort = TRUE) %>%
  print(n = Inf)
```

The resulting `cultures`, `culture_organisms`, and `ast_endpoints` data frames
will support organism mapping and phenotype classification in the next stage.
